{{Short description|German researcher}}

[[File: Lars Mathias Blank.jpg|thumb]]
'''Lars Mathias Blank,''' (born 27 November 1969 in [[Hilden]], Germany) is a German engineer, [[biologist]], and professor at [[RWTH Aachen University]], and head of its Institute of Applied Microbiology.

==Career==
Blank studied [[Chemical Engineering]] from 1990 to 1997 at the [[TU Dortmund University]] and Biology from 1992 to 1997 at the [[Ruhr University Bochum|Ruhr University of Bochum]] (Germany). For  his master's, he worked in [[Metabolic_engineering|Metabolic Engineering]] in the group of E. T. Papoutsakis at [[Northwestern University]] in Illinois, USA, and in yeast cell biology in the group of Prof. W.-H. Kunau at Ruhr University Bochum. For his Ph.D., he worked for  Prof. L. K. Nielsen at the Biotech Centre of the [[University of Queensland]], Australia (1998 to 2002), where he developed a continuous process for [[hyaluronic acid]] production using [[lactic acid]] bacteria. <ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-12-08 |publisher=RWTH Aachen University |title=Vita |url=https://www.iamb.rwth-aachen.de/cms/iamb/das-institut/team/gruppe-blank/institutsleiter/~qreim/lars-blank/?lidx=1&allou=1 |website=www.iamb.rwth-aachen.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> During his Ph.D., he worked as a visiting scientist at the [[Technical University of Denmark]] (DTU) in Lyngby, Denmark, from September to December 1999. From November 2004 until June 2011, Blank led the group 'Systems Biotechnology' at the Laboratory of Chemical Biotechnology of 
Prof. A. Schmid at the TU Dortmund University and was a senior research fellow at the [[Leibniz Institute]] of Analytical Sciences (ISAS) in Dortmund. In January 2010, he finalized his [[Habilitation]]. In July 2011, Blank became professor, chair of Applied Microbiology, and head of the Institute of Applied Microbiology (iAMB) at RWTH Aachen University. <ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-12-08 |publisher=RWTH Aachen University |title=About Institute of Applied Microbiology of RWTH Aachen |url=https://www.biologie.rwth-aachen.de/go/id/okxev#aaaaaaaaaaolffy/ |website=www.biologie.rwth-aachen.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Blank coordinated the EU project ‘P4SB – From plastic waste to plastic value using ''Pseudomonas putida'' [[Synthetic biology|Synthetic Biology]]‘ <ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-12-09 |publisher=RWTH Aachen University |title=P4SB Homepage |url=https://www.p4sb.eu/ |website=www.p4sb.eu}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and was the coordinator of the Horizon 2020 EU project ‘MIX-UP – Mixed plastics biodegradation and [[upcycling]] using microbial communities‘. <ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-12-09 |publisher=RWTH Aachen University |title=MIX-UP Homepage |url=https://www.mix-up.eu/ |website=www.mix-up.eu}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> He is partner of the Werner Siemens Foundation (WSS) <ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-12-12 |publisher=Werner Siemens Foundation |title=Werner Siemens Foundation |url=https://www.wernersiemens-stiftung.ch/en/ |website=www.wernersiemens-stiftung.ch/}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> century project 'catalaix', researching open loop [[plastic recycling]]. <ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-12-12 |publisher=Werner Siemens Foundation |title=Catalaix project of the WSS |url=https://www.wernersiemens-stiftung.ch/en/projects/catalaix |website=www.wernersiemens-stiftung.ch/}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

==Research==
In his research, Blank focuses on fundamental and applied aspects of microbial [[metabolism]]. <ref>{{cite web|access-date=2025-12-08 |publisher=RWTH Aachen University |title=iAMB Areas of Research |url=https://www.iamb.rwth-aachen.de/cms/iamb/Forschung/~kvzh/Forschungsgebiet/ |website=www.rwth-aachen.de}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> Of specific interest is the interaction between the metabolic network and the introduced genetic and environmental perturbations. Research on [[in silico]]/[[in vivo]] metabolic network operation aims to deepen understanding of cell function, with the ultimate goal of rational [[cell engineering]].
He is [[associate editor]] of renowned international journals such as ''Engineering in Life Sciences'', ''Microbial Biotechnology'', ''Fungal Biology and Biotechnology'', ''Journal of Bioscience and Bioengineering'', ''Metabolic Engineering'', and ''Metabolic Engineering Communication.''
